thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures in the Red on Trade Worries as G7 Summit Commences

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures in the Red on Trade Worries as G7 Summit Commences
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Friday's regular session:
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): +2.8%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.6%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.1%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.2%
VelocityShares Daily 2x VIX Short Term ETN ( TVIX ): +5.2%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including SPY, IWM and IVV were weaker. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was down 0.5%.
US stock futures were pointing to a negative open, as worries over the outcome to this weekend's Group of Seven meeting coupled with the continued meltdown in emerging markets and selling pressure on Apple (AAPL) elevated investors' risk aversion.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market activity.
Zumiez (ZUMZ) jumped more than 15% after the company reported a narrower-than-expected fiscal Q1 loss of $0.10 a share, better than the consensus on Capital IQ for a loss of $0.12 and the year earlier loss of $0.18. Total net sales were up 14% to $206.3 million, topping the Street's view for $199.3 million. Comparable sales rose 8.3% compared with growth of 1.8% a year earlier. Zumiez sees sales for the quarter ending Aug. 4 of $213 million to $217 million with comparable sales growth of between 3% and 5%. Earnings are seen between $0.04 and $0.09 per share. Analysts are projecting Q2 revenue of $202.1 million and a loss of $0.01 per share.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.1%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 0.6% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 0.3%.
Pzena Investment Management (PZN) said late Thursday that its assets under management were $37.10 billion as of May 31, up from $33.10 billion a year earlier but down slightly from $38.90 billion as of April 30. The current assets include $25.10 billion in the US and $12 billion outside the US.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) dropped almost 2% in pre-market trade after the Nikkei Asian Review said the company has asked its supply chain to prepare around 20% fewer components than in the year-ago period for iPhones debuting in the latter half of 2018. Apple last year placed orders to prepare for production of up to 100 million units of the new iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus and iPhone X, but this year Apple currently expects total shipments of only 80 million units for new models, two people reportedly told the publication. Apple's supply chain also was told to prepare earlier for the two OLED models, in hopes of avoiding a delay similar to last year's, two industry sources reportedly said.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.4%.
Seadrill (SDRL) rose more than 5% after it said it expects to emerge from the chapter 11 process in the first half of July. Existing Seadrill Limited will be wound up and the new company with the reorganized capital structure will assume its name. It said it plans to re-list the new company's common stock on both the New York Stock Exchange and the Oslo Stock Exchange as before, retaining the same ticker symbols. Listing for both exchanges is expected to occur in July.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.2%. Natural gas was down 2% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.8%.
Gold was down 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was down 0.2%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.4%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were flat. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 0.5%.
TrovaGene (TROV) fell more than 53% after the company said it priced an underwritten public offering of 18 million shares and warrants at $1 per share. Underwriters were granted a 45-day option to purchase up to 2.7 million additional shares. The company plans to use approximately $16.2 million in proceeds to fund its research and development and for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close on June 12.
